candidates.reaction_description: Proton transfer. A carbonyl O8 lone pair takes the acidic H from TFA O17, and the O17-H bond electrons stay on O17, giving trifluoroacetate. Bond formed: O8-H. Bond broken: O17-H. Charge stays balanced: the neutral pair becomes a cation plus an anion.

output.llm_reasoning: Acid-mediated Boc deprotection. The first elementary step is protonation of the carbamate carbonyl oxygen (O8) by TFA (O17-H). This gives the resonance-stabilized protonated carbamate and trifluoroacetate. Next steps: C12-O10 heterolysis to the tert-butyl cation and carbamic acid, E1 loss of a proton from the tert-butyl cation to isobutylene (the proton is taken up by trifluoroacetate, regenerating TFA), decarboxylation of the carbamic acid to CO2, and the final proton transfers that give the free amine.
